text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein on Monday visits Tafila governate in south of kingdom to tour civic centres and meet locals and community elders.
- Prime Minister Majali says in interview with a Kuwaiti daily that voting is national duty; stresses ties with Kuwait moving in right direction.
- Majali says Israeli intransigence is behind setback in Middle East peace process; says Jordanian ties with Syria and Iraq "good".
- Eighty independent personalities declare boycott of elections due in November; among names are two former prime ministers, Taher al-Masri and Ahmad Obeidat.
- Moslem Brotherhood head Abdul Majid Thunaibat says outcome of dialogue with government will determine movement's final position on whether to go ahead with decision to boycott elections.
- Crown prince's son, Prince Rashed, recuperating after car accident, expected to leave hospital in days.
